‹ Urgent eye care

Eye injuries and foreign body removal

We treat most eye injuries right here in our office.

Eye emergency? Call us right away at (918) 540-1929 for:

  • Sudden loss of vision, even if it comes back, or a new dark curtain or shadow across your vision
  • A chemical splash or burn to the eye
  • An object that has pierced the eye. Don't try to remove it or press on the eye.
  • A serious eye injury, including an injury from high-speed metal or debris, such as from grinding or hammering
  • Severe eye pain, especially with nausea or vomiting

Chemical splash: start rinsing your eye with clean running water right away, and keep rinsing for at least 15 minutes. Don't stop rinsing to call us.

If we're closed or you can't reach us, go to the nearest emergency room. Don't wait for a callback. Call 911 if you need an ambulance.

Other urgent eye problems? Call us for same-day care:

  • New flashes of light or floaters
  • A red or painful eye, especially if you wear contact lenses
  • A suspected scratch or something irritating the surface of your eye
  • New eye pain or vision changes not listed above

We'll ask about your symptoms and work you into our schedule as quickly as we can.

If we can't see you promptly, get immediate care from another eye doctor or an emergency department.

That includes removing foreign bodies such as metal, wood and dirt from the surface of the eye, removing rust rings left behind by metal foreign bodies, and treating scratches on the cornea, called corneal abrasions. More serious injuries may require emergency or surgical care.
